Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testPreserveDOM()` calls `doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, " foo ")`, which internally creates a JXPathContext using a DocumentContainer with the "DOM" model, pointing to an XML "XmlSpace.xml". The test checks that the XPath expression `"test/text[@id='preserve']"` yields the string `" foo "` with leading and trailing spaces preserved.

The bug report indicates that when retrieving XML values with leading or trailing spaces, JXPath automatically trims these spaces, causing the output to lose them, e.g. `<value> 12324 56</value>` is seen as `'1234 56'` rather than `' 1234 56'`.

From the code snippets:

- The DocumentContainer opens and parses the XML, and `getValue` returns the parsed DOM document.
- The DOMNodePointer's `getValue()` returns `stringValue(node)`.
  
Since the observed behavior is trimming of white spaces and no explicit code shown so far indicating preserving these spaces, the cause is likely that the code resolving text values from the DOM (e.g., stringValue) is normalizing or trimming text content, thereby removing leading and trailing spaces. This is a common issue when extracting content from XML nodes if normalization is applied or getTextContent() is called without preserving leading/trailing spaces.

Thus, the root cause is that the DOMNodePointer (or underlying code it calls to obtain string value) is automatically trimming whitespace from text nodes when retrieving the value. This behavior causes the test, which expects the spaces intact, to fail.

No recent issues are available to compare, but the current evidence points to missing preservation of whitespace in DOM node string value extraction. Fixes should ensure that leading and trailing spaces in text node values are preserved during value retrieval by JXPath.

Next, I will examine methods involved in string extraction from the DOM node, such as `stringValue()` or similar used by `getValue()` on DOMNodePointer to identify where the trimming might occur.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
